data.summary: Ruling. (1) A detached process may die or terminate under its own declared process semantics; detach removes supervisor cancellation/authority, not mortality. Add a general self-death/terminal transition available to root, attached, or detached instances only at a declared safe termination/failure point, with the exact outcome, obligation, custody, resource and observation disposition required by that process contract. Keep the supervised child-death transition for the extra parent notification/reaping relationship. The useful theorem becomes: an attached death uses the supervised form; any unsupervised death is root/detached self-death justified by its local terminal contract. Ordinary processes that never detach or expose a death point pay no extra field-by-field ceremony; standard constructors package the common case. (2) A complete runnable program network always retains exactly one root slot, even when that instance is terminal. Root uniqueness alone is insufficient. Rootless graphs remain legal only as composable process fragments, not as complete ProcessPlan/VerifiedProgram networks. Child restart must require the old and new incarnations to be attached under the same preserved parentage and cannot replace a root with a child. If root restart is supported, use a separate constructor that preserves `.root`. Add RootExists at the complete-network wrapper/plan boundary rather than burdening every fragment, plus negative fixtures for detached self-death without a declared safe point, child restart of a root, and completion of a rootless plan.

Ruling: ordinary Detaches applies only to a live/running attached instance. Do not use detach as corpse disposal: detachment relinquishes supervision while preserving a running incarnation, whereas disposal of a died child must be a distinct ReapsDeath/collect-death transition. That transition requires the exact died reason, the still-attached parent relationship, delivery/recording of the parent-facing death event, and complete disposition of the child's obligations, custody, escrow, and resources before freeing the slot; standard death constructors should package those proofs. Add the two-step childDied-then-detach witness as a negative fixture and a positive childDied-then-reap fixture. The earlier g-design:133 ruling is amended, not discarded: a future general SelfDies terminal transition remains required for root and detached instances at a declared safe death point, and its local terminal contract owns the complete disposition. Once SelfDies exists, the current dying_was_supervised theorem must narrow to supervised death constructors; the global classification theorem says every transition that newly creates .died is either supervised ChildDied or contract-justified SelfDies. Root may therefore die without losing its root slot. A detached died instance may later be collected only by its own explicit no-custody/no-obligation collection rule, never by pretending it was supervised.
